title: AppraiseAI
pitch: AI handles the evidence. You make the final call.
about_excerpt: AI handles the evidence. You make the final call. Like Comment Story Updates App Cover WebMCP tools Inspiration Appraisal work is meaningful, but the process around it can be frustrating and repetitive. Organizing field notes, saving evidence, researching comparable sales, checking completeness, and verifying that every conclusion is supported can take attention away from the work that matters most: professional judgment. The idea for AppraiseAI started when I saw OpenAI’s tweet about WebMCP. I was curious, so I began reading more about it. The more I learned, the more I saw how well WebMCP could fit this problem. Instead of making appraisers copy information between a website and a chatbot, I wanted to create one shared workspace where people and AI agents could work together while keeping the final decision firmly in human hands. What it does AppraiseAI turns unstructured field notes and object images into an organized, evidence-backed appraisal draft, saving professionals valuable time to focus on expert judgment and final decisions. An AI agent can: Read the active appraisal context Turn field notes into structured appraisal items Search a catalog of synthetic comparable sales Link relevant evidence to each item Draft supported valuation ranges Check whether the appraisal is ready for review Hand the completed draft back to the appraiser Every agent action immediately appears in the visible interface, updates the appraisal version, and is recorded in an activity ledger. How I built it AppraiseAI is built with React, Vite, and TypeScript. The application uses a shared, typed state layer persisted in localStorage . The visible interface and WebMCP tools both use the same domain operations and validation rules, ensuring that an agent cannot bypass restrictions enforced by the application. The page exposes eight focused WebMCP tools through document.modelContext.registerTool() : get_appraisal_context add_appraisal_items update_appraisal_item search_comparable_sales link_comparable_sale set_item_valuation get_appraisal_readiness mark_appraisal_ready_for_review Every successful mutation returns a verification snapshot so the agent can confirm what changed. The demo requires no backend, accounts, uploads, or external APIs. All cases, objects, images, comparable sales, people, organizations, dates, and values were created specifically for this challenge and are entirely fictional. Challenges I ran into Finding out in two days what WebMCP is and what WebMCP does. Maintaining an agent and an interface that always work together. Each action on the tool would trigger a new state version, update the workspace at once, save the change locally, and generate a traceable activity entry. Another crucial point was ensuring the application would keep working in browsers without WebMCP support. Lastly, making sure the demo video is less than three minutes long. Accomplishments that i'm proud of I am especially proud that AppraiseAI demonstrates a complete human-agent workflow rather than a collection of disconnected tool calls. The agent can structure notes, research evidence, draft valuation ranges, identify missing work, and prepare the appraisal for review all inside the same interface the appraiser uses. What I learned WebMCP tools are surprisingly easy to build, yet they can save people enormous amounts of time. They can act as a second brain or personal assistant, taking care of repetitive work so people can focus on what actually requires their expertise. What's next for AppraiseAI The next step is to explore how AppraiseAI could support larger, more flexible appraisal workflows while preserving the same principles of human control. This could include additional components for customer communication, report generation, and further automation of repetitive tasks. live_observation.after_state: The page remained visually unchanged: the draft still said No objects structured yet and Mark ready for review remained disabled.
